records.definition: Reusable computation with parameters and a result boundary.
constraints: The structural concept is independent of any one programming language.
Every language syntax that expresses it is a syntax alias of the concept.

records.definition: A rule for an enumeration variant, the construct the upstream grammar names enum_variant.
constraints: Only the native Rust grammar defines this construct.
js/scripts/import-native-grammars.mjs generates this record from the rule names of the imported grammars.

records.definition: The side effects a program performs, such as input, output and mutation.
constraints: Each language frontend reports evidence for this construct or states why it is unavailable.

records.definition: The macros and custom notation a program defines or uses.
constraints: Each language frontend reports evidence for this construct or states why it is unavailable.

records.definition: A closed algebraic data type: finitely many constructors with fixed field types, possibly recursive.
constraints: No meta-language concept record has this exact meaning; RML mints it under the rml namespace until an upstream record exists.
Records, structures and struct variants reach a certificate as data types after RML surface lowering.

records.definition: One constructor of a closed algebraic data type, applied to exactly its fields.
constraints: No meta-language concept record has this exact meaning; RML mints it under the rml namespace until an upstream record exists.

records.definition: A named proposition that a certificate either discharges by RML evaluation or keeps as an open obligation.
constraints: No meta-language concept record has this exact meaning; RML mints it under the rml namespace until an upstream record exists.
A theorem is never discharged by a target kernel; kernels are oracles.

records.definition: A closed condition main checks while it runs; RML discharges it by running main or refutes it when main aborts on it.
constraints: No meta-language concept record has this exact meaning; RML mints it under the rml namespace until an upstream record exists.

records.definition: A statement an emitter relies on that the certificate lists and never discharges.
constraints: No meta-language concept record has this exact meaning; RML mints it under the rml namespace until an upstream record exists.

records.definition: The obligation that every call of a recursive function returns.
constraints: No meta-language concept record has this exact meaning; RML mints it under the rml namespace until an upstream record exists.
Discharged only by an RML structural-decrease derivation that agrees with the archive.

records.definition: A step of the translation that is trusted host code, recorded as an open obligation instead of hidden.
constraints: No meta-language concept record has this exact meaning; RML mints it under the rml namespace until an upstream record exists.

records.definition: A closed goal is decided by RML evaluating the certified intermediate program.
constraints: No meta-language concept record has this exact meaning; RML mints it under the rml namespace until an upstream record exists.

records.definition: Termination follows from a parameter that RML finds structurally smaller on every recursive call, as the archive also records.
constraints: No meta-language concept record has this exact meaning; RML mints it under the rml namespace until an upstream record exists.

records.definition: A closed goal that RML has not evaluated, so it stays open.
constraints: No meta-language concept record has this exact meaning; RML mints it under the rml namespace until an upstream record exists.

records.definition: A goal left to a target proof kernel, whose acceptance is oracle evidence and never an RML discharge.
constraints: No meta-language concept record has this exact meaning; RML mints it under the rml namespace until an upstream record exists.

records.definition: A goal checked by running a bounded executable test, which is not a proof.
constraints: No meta-language concept record has this exact meaning; RML mints it under the rml namespace until an upstream record exists.

records.definition: An obligation that holds by assumption and is listed as assumed.
constraints: No meta-language concept record has this exact meaning; RML mints it under the rml namespace until an upstream record exists.

records.definition: Recursion without a structurally decreasing parameter, or through a call cycle, whose termination is not proved.
constraints: No meta-language concept record has this exact meaning; RML mints it under the rml namespace until an upstream record exists.

records.definition: A goal observed by native toolchains in continuous integration, which is oracle evidence only.
constraints: No meta-language concept record has this exact meaning; RML mints it under the rml namespace until an upstream record exists.

records.definition: The ordered observable output of a program and whether it completes or aborts.
constraints: No meta-language concept record has this exact meaning; RML mints it under the rml namespace until an upstream record exists.

records.definition: The discipline that governs who owns, borrows and drops a value.
constraints: No meta-language concept record has this exact meaning; RML mints it under the rml namespace until an upstream record exists.

records.definition: The types a program declares and checks.
constraints: No meta-language concept record has this exact meaning; RML mints it under the rml namespace until an upstream record exists.
meta-language program.types-and-universes joins types with universes; RML keeps the two dimensions distinct, so neither reuses it.

records.definition: The universe hierarchy the declared types live in.
constraints: No meta-language concept record has this exact meaning; RML mints it under the rml namespace until an upstream record exists.
meta-language program.types-and-universes joins types with universes; RML keeps the two dimensions distinct, so neither reuses it.

records.definition: The statements a translation relies on without proving them.
constraints: No meta-language concept record has this exact meaning; RML mints it under the rml namespace until an upstream record exists.

records.definition: The goals a translation must discharge, with their discharge status.
constraints: No meta-language concept record has this exact meaning; RML mints it under the rml namespace until an upstream record exists.
meta-language program.proof-terms-and-tactics names the proofs a program writes, not the goals a translation owes.

records.definition: Type classes and traits that select an implementation by type.
constraints: No meta-language concept record has this exact meaning; RML mints it under the rml namespace until an upstream record exists.

records.definition: Host runtime code outside the certified program.
constraints: No meta-language concept record has this exact meaning; RML mints it under the rml namespace until an upstream record exists.

records.definition: Proof kernels and compilers outside RML.
constraints: No meta-language concept record has this exact meaning; RML mints it under the rml namespace until an upstream record exists.

records.definition: The checker whose verdict discharges an obligation.
constraints: No meta-language concept record has this exact meaning; RML mints it under the rml namespace until an upstream record exists.

records.definition: A product type with named or positional fields, lowered to a single-constructor data type with one accessor per field read.
constraints: No meta-language concept record has this exact meaning; RML mints it under the rml namespace until an upstream record exists.
A Rust struct or tuple struct, a Lean structure and a Rocq record share this concept.

records.definition: A value of a record type written with its fields, lowered to the constructor applied to the fields in declaration order.
constraints: No meta-language concept record has this exact meaning; RML mints it under the rml namespace until an upstream record exists.

records.definition: The read of one field of a record value, lowered to a call of a generated accessor.
constraints: No meta-language concept record has this exact meaning; RML mints it under the rml namespace until an upstream record exists.

records.definition: A pattern that names fields of a record, lowered to a positional constructor pattern with wildcards for omitted fields.
constraints: No meta-language concept record has this exact meaning; RML mints it under the rml namespace until an upstream record exists.

records.definition: A constructor of a data type whose fields are named, lowered to a positional constructor.
constraints: No meta-language concept record has this exact meaning; RML mints it under the rml namespace until an upstream record exists.

records.definition: A declaration with explicit type parameters, copied once per explicit instantiation under a fresh name.
constraints: No meta-language concept record has this exact meaning; RML mints it under the rml namespace until an upstream record exists.
Only explicit instantiations are monomorphized; inference, bounds and universe parameters are refused.

records.definition: A use of a generic declaration with its type arguments written out, lowered to the monomorphized copy.
constraints: No meta-language concept record has this exact meaning; RML mints it under the rml namespace until an upstream record exists.
